thought.text: Part 1 was lost (the harness intermittently drops writes during glitch bursts). Let me write + verify + run in a single command:

reasoning_content:
Part 1 failed to persist again (the `OUT` on line 2 is undefined — meaning the first write, which was reported as "part1 ok", had been lost!). The harness is intermittently discarding file writes. This is serious: my writes to /tmp are sometimes being lost.

Wait — "part1 ok" was echoed, so at that point the command should have succeeded... and yet now /tmp/fa.sh only has parts 2+3 (starting from the loc= line?). Line 2 = "loc=$(curl...)" → $OUT is undefined on line 2... so part 1 (the OUT= line) wasn't in the file. Hmm, but part 1 was echoed as ok.

Could it be... that part 1's write went through, but then a later burst of podman glitches wiped /tmp? Or maybe the glitch corrupts things at the FUSE/overlay layer.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the harness's command execution itself is unstable: the command that was executed isn't necessarily the one I sent (some commands fail with "Podman" and don't execute at all). When "part1 ok" was displayed, the write had been performed. Then the part 2 write was appended. Then the part 3 write was "appended"... and yet now the file is missing part 1's lines?

Hmm, looking at the actual error lines: line 2 = loc (part 2's first line), line 3 = echo step1... but part 3's line 10 is the final cat. If part 1 existed, the file would have been 5 + 5 + 10 = 20 lines, and line 2 would be the eval line. The errors show $OUT being undefined on lines 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 — consistent with part 1 being missing (4 lines: shebang, cd, eval, JAR/OUT). So the file = part 2 + part 3, and part 1 has been lost.

So: part 1's write was lost, even though it was reported as successful. The harness's /tmp writes are unreliable during glitch bursts.

Solution: use the repository directory (/workspace) instead of /tmp, and write to a single file per command, then verify immediately within the same command (write + cat + execute in one command to minimize the gap). If verification shows the content is wrong, retry.

Also, regarding the intermittent command failures: retry until it works.

Let's do a single command that writes the complete script, verifies (wc -l + head), and executes it.

action.command:
cat > /tmp/fa.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
cd /workspace
eval $(grep -E "^(LOCAL_USER_EMAIL|LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD)=" .env | sed "s/^/export /")
JAR=/tmp/fa-cookies.txt; OUT=/tmp/fa.out; : > $OUT; rm -f "$JAR"
loc=$(curl -sS -c $JAR -o /dev/null -w "%{redirect_url}" "http://localhost:3000/app/" 2>>$OUT)
echo "step1=$loc" >> $OUT
[ -z "$loc" ] && { echo FAIL-redirect >> $OUT; cat $OUT; exit 1; }
code=$(curl -sS -b $JAR -c $JAR -o /tmp/fa-login.html -w "%{http_code}" "$loc" 2>>$OUT)
echo "step2=$code" >> $OUT
ACTION=$(grep -oE "<form id=\"kc-form-login\"[^>]*action=\"[^\"]*\"" /tmp/fa-login.html | sed "s/.*action=\"//;s/\"$//;s/&/\\&/g")
res=$(curl -sS -b $JAR -c $JAR -o /tmp/fa-login2.html -w "%{http_code}|%{redirect_url}" -X POST "$ACTION" --data-urlencode "username=$LOCAL_USER_EMAIL" --data-urlencode "password=$LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD" --data-urlencode "signup=false" 2>>$OUT)
echo "step3=$res" >> $OUT
CB=$(echo "$res" | cut -d"|" -f2)
res4=$(curl -sS -b $JAR -c $JAR -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}|%{redirect_url}" "$CB" 2>>$OUT)
echo "step4=$res4" >> $OUT
APP=$(echo "$res4" | cut -d"|" -f2)
code5=$(curl -sS -b $JAR -c $JAR -o /tmp/fa-app.html -w "%{http_code}" "$APP" 2>>$OUT)
echo "step5=$code5" >> $OUT
echo "title=$(grep -oE "<title>[^<]*" /tmp/fa-app.html | head -1)" >> $OUT
cat $OUT
SCRIPT
wc -l /tmp/fa.sh && head -4 /tmp/fa.sh && bash /tmp/fa.sh
